[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Materialized Views in Oracle Database"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Materialized views are schema objects that contain the results of a query. They are like tables, but the data they hold is derived from the base tables or other views. Oracle automatically maintains materialized views to reflect changes to the underlying data, unless they are configured otherwise."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Purpose of Materialized Views"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Improve query performance: By pre-calculating and storing query results, materialized views can significantly reduce query response times, especially for complex queries or queries against large datasets."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Data warehousing: Materialized views are commonly used in data warehousing environments to create summary tables and aggregate data for reporting and analysis."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Replication: Materialized views can be used to replicate data between databases, allowing for distributed data access and disaster recovery."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating Materialized Views"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"The basic syntax for creating a materialized view is as follows:"},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_name
REFRESH [COMPLETE | FAST | FORCE] 
[ON [COMMIT | DEMAND]]
[START WITH date]
[NEXT date]
AS
select_statement;"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Let's break down the key components:"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"mv_name: The name of the materialized view."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"REFRESH: Specifies how the materialized view is refreshed. COMPLETE refreshes the entire view, FAST uses materialized view logs to refresh only changed data, and FORCE attempts a FAST refresh and falls back to COMPLETE if FAST is not possible."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ON COMMIT: Refreshes the materialized view whenever a transaction commits that affects the underlying tables."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ON DEMAND: Refreshes the materialized view only when explicitly requested using the DBMS_MVIEW.REFRESH procedure."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"START WITH and NEXT: Specifies the initial refresh time and the interval for subsequent refreshes when using ON DEMAND."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"select_statement: The query that defines the data to be stored in the materialized view."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Example"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW sales_summary
REFRESH COMPLETE
ON DEMAND
START WITH SYSDATE
NEXT SYSDATE + 1
AS
SELECT prod_category, SUM(sales_amount) AS total_sales
FROM sales_table
GROUP BY prod_category;"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"This example creates a materialized view named 'sales_summary' that summarizes sales data by product category. It is refreshed completely on demand, starting immediately and then every day."},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Materialized View Logs"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"For FAST refresh to work, you need to create materialized view logs on the base tables. The materialized view log tracks changes to the base table, allowing Oracle to refresh the materialized view incrementally."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW LOG ON sales_table
WITH ROWID, SEQUENCE (prod_category, sales_amount)
INCLUDING NEW VALUES;"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"This creates a materialized view log on the 'sales_table', tracking changes to the 'prod_category' and 'sales_amount' columns. The 'WITH ROWID' clause is generally recommended. 'INCLUDING NEW VALUES' stores the new values of the columns after an update."},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Refreshing Materialized Views"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can manually refresh a materialized view using the 'DBMS_MVIEW.REFRESH' procedure:"},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"EXECUTE DBMS_MVIEW.REFRESH('sales_summary');"},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"To refresh all materialized views in a schema, you can use:"},{"order":28,"type":"code","text":"EXECUTE DBMS_MVIEW.REFRESH_ALL_MVIEWS;"},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"Considerations"},{"order":30,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Storage: Materialized views consume storage space, so consider the size of the data being stored."},{"order":31,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Refresh frequency: Balance the need for up-to-date data with the overhead of refreshing the materialized view. Frequent refreshes can impact performance."},{"order":32,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Query rewrite: Oracle can automatically rewrite queries to use materialized views, even if the query doesn't explicitly reference them. This can significantly improve performance without requiring changes to application code. Ensure query rewrite is enabled ('QUERY_REWRITE_ENABLED = TRUE' and 'QUERY_REWRITE_INTEGRITY = TRUSTED' in the database parameters)."},{"order":33,"type":"subheading","text":"Dropping Materialized Views"},{"order":34,"type":"paragraph","text":"To drop a materialized view, use the following command:"},{"order":35,"type":"code","text":"DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_name;"}]
